intro: Converting ml to grams requires accounting for ingredient bulk density because ml measure kitchen volume while grams measure mass. In professional baking and culinary formulation, 1 US cup of water weighs 236.59 grams, 1 US cup of all-purpose flour weighs 120 grams, and 1 US cup of granulated sugar weighs 200 grams. Use our ingredient-aware calculator and reference table below to convert recipes accurately without kitchen scale guesswork.

mistakesAndEdgeCases.title: Ingredient Density & US vs. Metric Cup Differences
items: Never assume 1 cup or 1 mL weighs the same across dry ingredients: 1 US cup of all-purpose flour is ~120 g, whereas 1 US cup of honey is ~340 g.
US recipe cups equal 236.59 mL (or 240 mL FDA label), while Australian/Commonwealth metric cups equal 250 mL.

formula.standardNote: Verified against USDA FoodData Central and King Arthur Baking weight charts.

faqs.question: Why does converting ml to grams require selecting an ingredient?
faqs.answer: Because ml measure three-dimensional space (volume) and grams measure weight (mass). Denser ingredients like butter or honey weigh significantly more per ml than aerated powders like flour or cocoa.

faqs.question: How many grams are in 1 US cup vs 1 tablespoon of flour and sugar?
faqs.answer: 1 US cup of all-purpose flour weighs 120 g (7.5 g per tablespoon), while 1 US cup of granulated white sugar weighs 200 g (12.5 g per tablespoon).
